Every year I buy ONE hydroponically grown basil plant from the grocery store, and take cuttings. Then, once those cuttings are somewhat established, I repeat until I have as many plants as I want! It's *really *easy, and it works! There's plenty of info out there on how to do this, but this is what I've found to work really well for me.

Tips:

  • cut stems to a length of 2-3 inches. make sure you have some leaves up top. shorter is sometimes better in this regard because it will develop roots quicker and is less prone to wind/water damage after transplanting b/c it's nice and low to the ground.

  • put in water at least 1/2 an inch, no more than an inch. the more stem in the water, the longer it takes to root.

  • don't let leaves sit in water - they'll rot. i usually put 3-4 stems in each cup (the roots don't get tangled easily, so it's cool), and have the leaves all kinda supporting/resting on each other as well as the rim of the cup to prevent them from going in the water.

  • if a stem is turning black at the bottom, it's rot. take it out and cut it off. change the water and put it in a cup by itself. if it happens again, throw it out. plenty of cuttings to go around.

  • change water every couple of days, especially in the beginning. use cold water. I tend to think when the water gets hot, it slows the rooting process.

  • keep the cuttings on a window sill that gets a good amount of light

  • use a see through cup. for some reason it also works better

  • when transplanting, take the water the cuttings were in and incorporate it into the fresh water you use to "water-in" the plants.

  • and last but not least: Do not plant if there is a chance of frost. I planted a bunch in late march and they all died! lol
